nodes.title: The genuine nonabelian example: a 60-torsion Bloch class over a quartic field
nodes.statement: For A = (8 5; 5 4), symmetric positive definite (det 7), the Nahm equations 1 − z_1 = z_1⁸z_2⁵, 1 − z_2 = z_1⁵z_2⁴ have eight solutions in two Galois orbits. The first orbit is z_1⁴ + z_1³ + 3z_1² − 3z_1 − 1 = 0 with z_2 = (−9z_1³ − 6z_1² − 25z_1 + 37)/5, giving the field F of discriminant −5²·19 = −475, signature (2,1) and Galois group D4. The second is z_1⁴ − z_1³ + 3z_1² − 3z_1 + 1 = 0 with z_2 = z_1³ + 3z_1, giving E of discriminant 229, signature (0,2) and Galois group S4. The polynomial (257) has discriminant −5⁴·19 and index 5 in O_F; this explains GSWZ's second value −5⁴·19 (source issue E50). The distinguished solution (0.884829012582553…, 0.789393691312840…) lies in a real embedding of F and is non-degenerate: δ = (753 − 505z_1 − 124z_1² − 186z_1³)/5, which agrees with (36), with N(δ) = 5²·19². Its class ξ = [z_1] + [z_2] ∈ B(F) is torsion: the Bloch–Wigner sum vanishes at the complex place, and L(ξ) = π²/15 in CGZ's normalisation at both real places. GSWZ say its order is 60. The asymptotic series is f̂_1(x) = e^{π²/(15 log(1+x))}δ^{-1/2}(1 + a_1x + a_2x² + a_3x³ + O(x⁴)) with a_1 = (−1284z_1³ + 384z_1² − 5520z_1 + 2047)/(2²·3·5²·19²), a_2 = (−3084024z_1³ − 11262336z_1² − 1073760z_1 + 17201653)/(2⁵·3²·5²·19⁴), a_3 = (−1185017476284z_1³ + 1129707725184z_1² − 5869777630320z_1 + 1818824190547)/(2⁷·3⁴·5⁴·19⁶) (GSWZ (261)-(262)), where F_0(q) ∼ f̂_1(q^{-1} − 1) (GSWZ (260) prints (1 + x)^{-1} + 1, source issue E51). Excluded primes: 2, 3, 5, 19, and the primes of CGZ's M_F used by Theorem 5. By HB.9/torsion-powers-lie-in-the-ring, (f_{A,z,ν})^{60} ∈ H_{O_F[1/Δ]} for all ν (δ is a unit there). GSWZ state 'H_{O_F[1/(5·19)]}, conjecturally, but provably if we invert 6', which presumes M_F has no prime outside {2, 3, 5, 19}; that is not checked here. GSWZ conjecture that 2 and 3 need not be inverted. The class of E is not torsion (Bloch–Wigner sums ±1.18968, ±1.69281), and its series shows no Δ-integrality.
hypotheses: A is symmetric positive definite with integer entries; the two quartic fields are the ones displayed; the distinguished solution lies in the first.
The 60-torsion is a computation in the Bloch group, verified by the numerical vanishing of the Bloch-Wigner evaluations and certifiable by five-term certificates.
The Habiro membership of the sixtieth power is stated by the source as conjectural in general and provable after inverting 6; this packet records that status and does not claim more.
proofSteps: Solve the equations and identify the two Galois orbits and the two quartic fields.
Locate the distinguished solution numerically and identify the real embedding it lies in.
Compute the Bloch class and its order, by the regulator criterion and by a five-term certificate.
Compute the asymptotic series numerically to high order, accelerate, and recognise the coefficients as algebraic numbers; the source displays delta and the first three coefficients.

Check the denominators: to order 27 the denominator is 2^77 times 3^40 times 5^34 times 19^52, so the series is Delta-integral; after raising to the sixtieth power the denominator improves to 5^33 times 19^54.
Repeat for the eight descendants that span the q-holonomic module, and for the second quartic field, where no such integrality appears.
acceptance: PARI: resultant of the Nahm system in z_1 = z_1^{24}·(the two quartics); nfdisc(F) = −475, poldisc(257) = −5⁴·19; nfdisc(E) = 229; N(δ) = 5²·19².
Bloch–Wigner: D(σz_1) + D(σz_2) = 0 (to 10^{−75}) at the complex place of F; in CGZ's normalisation L(z_1) + L(z_2) = π²/15 at both real places; so e^{π²/(15 log(1+x))} is the leading factor.
The denominators to order 27 are 2^77·3^40·5^34·19^52, improving to 5^33·19^54 for the 60-th power (GSWZ); the second orbit is the non-example.

nodes.title: The knot matrices, and the boundary between a formal series and a topological invariant
nodes.statement: Three formal Nahm data reproduce the perturbative series of the three simplest hyperbolic knots (GSWZ Remark 4.2). A_{4_1} = (1 1; 1 1): the Nahm equations force z_1 = z_2 = z with z² − z + 1 = 0, so z = ζ_6, K = Q(√−3), δ = (2 − z)/z = −√−3 and ξ = 2[ζ_6], with Bloch–Wigner value 2.0298832128 = vol(4_1). A_{5_2} = (2 1 1; 1 1 0; 1 0 1): the solution field is the cubic field of discriminant −23 (with u = 1 − z_1, u³ − u² + 2u − 1 = 0). A_{(−2,3,7)} = (1 0 1; 0 1 2; 1 2 4): the solution scheme has a component over the same cubic field (v³ − v + 1 = 0) and one over Q(2cos(2π/7)) (v³ − 2v² − v + 1 = 0, discriminant 49). From an ideal triangulation with Neumann–Zagier matrices (A|B) and B^{-1}A integral, A_Nahm = I − B^{-1}A. For these data the theorems of this roadmap give membership of an explicit series in an explicit Habiro module. They do NOT give that the series is a topological invariant, that it is independent of the triangulation, that it computes a Chern–Simons quantity, or that the knot invariant is quantum modular. Those are ArithmeticQuantumTopology's (QT.5 for triangulations and Pachner moves, QT.6 for the state-integral identification, QT.7 for quantum modularity), which import this roadmap and not conversely.
hypotheses: The three matrices are those recorded by the source; the general recipe requires the integrality of B inverse times A, which may fail for a given triangulation.
The corresponding solutions of the Nahm equations come from solutions of the gluing equations of the triangulation, which is where the geometry enters.
The boundary statement is the one the layer's own text insists on and is recorded as a node so that no later work can elide it.
proofSteps: Record the three matrices and check that each is symmetric and integral.
Record the recipe from a Neumann-Zagier datum, with its integrality condition.
Apply the membership theorem to obtain the module statement for each of the three.

State explicitly the four assertions that are NOT obtained, and for each name the kind of theorem that would be needed: invariance under the Pachner moves for triangulation independence, a comparison with the state integral for the Chern-Simons identification, and a quantum-modularity theorem for the asymptotic statement.
Record that ArithmeticQuantumTopology is the consumer of these series and must prove those statements itself.
acceptance: The figure-eight matrix is not positive definite, so it is a formal and not an analytic datum; the corresponding solution comes from the geometry and not from the cube.
The integrality condition on the Neumann-Zagier datum can fail, in which case the recipe gives nothing and a different quad type must be chosen.
Membership in a Habiro module is compatible with the series being a topological invariant and does not prove it; the two statements have different content.

nodes.title: The p-adic computations and the Frobenius by Hensel lifting
nodes.statement: The p-adic side of the examples is computed by Hensel lifting: if xi generates K with minimal polynomial P and p is unramified, then lifting the factorisation of P modulo p lifts the Frobenius of the residue field to an automorphism of the p-completion of R, and the lifting is constructive. The source uses this to compute the Frobenius endomorphism explicitly and to check the gluing conditions numerically, and gives a worked example illustrating the isomorphism between the p-adic K-theory of a local field and p^2 times its ring of integers.
hypotheses: p is unramified in K and greater than 3; R is O_K[1/Delta].
The Hensel lifting is the standard constructive one, by induction on the p-adic precision.
The worked example is Example 4.3 of the source, which illustrates Theorem 9.
proofSteps: Record the Hensel lifting argument and its constructive form.
Record the computation of the Frobenius as the lift of the p-power map.
Record the worked example and what it checks, namely the isomorphism given by the p-adic dilogarithm and the generation of the K-group by the classes of roots of unity.
Record that these computations are numerical verifications and not proofs of the theorems; the source says every result of the paper has been numerically verified.
acceptance: For K the cubic field of discriminant -23 and a small unramified p, the Frobenius is computed by lifting the factorisation of z^3 - z + 1.
The verification is of the gluing condition at a specific p and m, not of the theorem.
A numerical verification at finitely many primes is not a proof; this node records the distinction.

nodes.title: Modular examples: a quadratic Gauss sum and the symmetrised Rogers-Ramanujan function
nodes.statement: Two examples show what modularity contributes. The quadratic Gauss sum gives the collection F_m = (sum over k modulo m of zeta_m^{k^2})(sum over k of zeta_m^{-k^2})/m, which equals 1 for m congruent to 1 or 3 modulo 4, 0 for m congruent to 2 and 2 for m divisible by 4, and is an almost trivial element of the Habiro ring with 2 inverted; the variant with a fourth root of unity gives a slightly less trivial element over the ring with i and 1/2. The Rogers-Ramanujan example is genuinely arithmetic: the function J(z,q), a one-variable deformation, has the property that its expansion at zeta_m lies in an explicit localisation, and the residues over the m-th roots of the golden-ratio unit give constants F_m(u) in the field generated by the square root of 5 and the m-th roots of unity, whose first values the source lists.
hypotheses: The examples are those of GSWZ Section 4.7; the Rogers-Ramanujan field is the real quadratic field of the golden ratio, whose Galois group over the rationals is abelian.
Both examples produce elements of Habiro rings of small fields, which are the easiest non-trivial instances of the whole theory.
The lesson recorded is that modularity produces special elements associated to torsion classes in the third K-group, and that an abelian field is the easy case.
proofSteps: Compute the Gauss sum collection and check the four cases modulo 4.
Record the variant with the fourth root of unity and the ring it lives over.
Record the deformation J(z,q) of the Rogers-Ramanujan function and the localisation in which its expansion lies.
Compute the residues over the m-th roots of the golden-ratio unit and record the first values, which are constants in the field generated by the square root of 5.
Record the lesson: these are the abelian examples, and the quartic example of the previous node is the point of the theory, being genuinely nonabelian.
acceptance: The Gauss sum element is almost trivial, taking only the values 0, 1 and 2.
The Rogers-Ramanujan constants F_1 and F_2 are minus one half minus or plus the square root of 5 over 10.

These examples cannot replace the nonabelian one: the layer text asks for a genuine nonabelian number-field example, and the abelian cases do not exhibit the phenomena that the Frobenius gluing is designed for.

nodes.title: The pair of the knot 5_2 and the (-2,3,7)-pretzel knot over the cubic field of discriminant minus twenty-three
nodes.statement: The knots 5_2 and (−2,3,7) have common trace field K = Q(α), α³ − α² + 1 = 0, of discriminant −23 (their Nahm schemes: 5_2 reduces to u³ − u² + 2u − 1 = 0, u = 1 − z_1, with u ∈ K; (−2,3,7) has the components v³ − v + 1 = 0 over K and v³ − 2v² − v + 1 = 0 over Q(2cos(2π/7))). They are scissors congruent, so their Bloch classes agree modulo 6-torsion. Their series at m = 1 are computed by formal Gaussian integration of one-dimensional state integrals (400 coefficients). The product f^{(5_2)}_1(x)·f^{(−2,3,7)}_1(−x/(1+x)) has denominators only at 2 and 23 (x^400: 2^1997·23^581). Its constant term is the product of the inverse square roots of the two δ-invariants, c = 1/√(−6α² + 10α − 4)·1/√(−24α² + 32α − 26). Since −24α² + 32α − 26 = −2(2α² − 2α + 3)², c = ±1/(√(−2)·(2α² − 2α + 3)·√(−6α² + 10α − 4)). GSWZ (280)'s further equality c = 1/(√2·(2α² − 2α + 3)) is false (source issue E52). By GSWZ Proposition 1.5(b) (HabiroNumberFields:HB.7/involution-pairing) the two series are H_R-proportional after the scalar extension adjoining both square roots, although no simpler relation was found. The coefficients of the 5_2 series lie in K, while those of the (−2,3,7) series as GSWZ compute it also involve Q(2cos(2π/7)).
hypotheses: The trace field is the cubic field of discriminant -23; alpha satisfies alpha^3 - alpha^2 + 1 = 0.
The 5_2 Gaussian integral is the displayed one-dimensional integral with delta = 3 alpha - 2, and the first coefficients are the ones the source lists.
The computations are numerical or exact-arithmetic verifications, not proofs; the source says every result of the paper has been numerically verified.
proofSteps: Record the two knots, their common trace field and their scissors congruence, and the consequence for their Bloch classes modulo 6-torsion.
Record the three computational routes and the reduction of the state integrals to one dimension.
Record the product series with its denominators and its constant term, which is the strongest integrality observation in the source.
Record the difference between the two series through the etale algebras their coefficients generate.
Record the explicit Gaussian integral for 5_2 and the first coefficients, so that an implementation can be checked against them.
acceptance: The x^400 denominator 2^1997·23^581 of the product is the source's integrality test.
PARI: −24α² + 32α − 26 = −2(2α² − 2α + 3)²; at α = −0.754877666 the middle expression of (280) is −0.0323520 and the right side 0.1251641, so the printed equality fails.
From the coefficients of (282) (δ = 3α − 2), 2a_2 − a_1² = (465α² − 465α + 54)/23³, the x² coefficient of (283) (PARI).

nodes.title: Rank-one product identities as a check of the conventions
nodes.statement: For N = 1 and GSWZ's normalisation (31), F_A(t, q) = Σ_n (−1)^{An}q^{(An² + An)/2}t^n/(q; q)_n, the following hold. (i) A = 0: F_0(t, q) = (t; q)_∞^{-1} (Euler; printed in GSWZ §1.6); its DT exponents are c_{1,0} = −1 and all others 0. (ii) A = 1: F_1(t, q) = (qt; q)_∞ (Euler); c_{1,1} = 1 and all others 0. (iii) Both satisfy the q-difference equation (33), F(t) − F(qt) = (−1)^A t q^A F(q^A t). (iv) A = 3: z(t) = ∏_{n≥1}(1 − t^n)^{−n Σ_i c_{n,i}} (GSWZ (244)), where z(t) solves 1 − z = −tz³ and the c_{n,i} are the DT exponents of F_3; with GSWZ (236), Σ_i c_{n,i} = 1, 1, 3, 10, 40, 171 for n = 1, …, 6. A sign or exponent error in (31) or (33) breaks (i)-(iii); an error in the product expansion (28) breaks (iv).
hypotheses: N = 1; A ∈ {0, 1} for (i)-(iii) and A = 3 for (iv).
(iv) uses the exponents of GSWZ (236), which HB.8/acceptance-rank-one records, and the product expansion of HB.8/product-expansion-and-dt-exponents.
proofSteps: (i), (ii): Euler's identities, or the q-difference equation (33) with F(0, q) = 1 and its uniqueness (HB.8/series-F-A).
(iii): substitute into (33).
(iv): GSWZ (64): the limit q → 1 of F(qt, q)/F(t, q) is z(t), and the product expansion (28) gives the exponents.
acceptance: PARI: F_0 = (t; q)_∞^{-1} and F_1 = (qt; q)_∞ to t^8 and q^25; (33) holds for A = 0, …, 4 to t^8.
PARI: ∏_{n ≤ 6}(1 − t^n)^{−n s_n} with s = (1, 1, 3, 10, 40, 171) equals 1 + t + 3t² + 12t³ + 55t⁴ + 273t⁵ + 1428t⁶ + O(t⁷), the solution of 1 − z = −tz³ (GSWZ (239)).
With q^{An²/2} in place of q^{(An² + An)/2}, F_1 is no longer (qt; q)_∞, so this test catches the most likely normalisation error.

nodes.title: The abelian worked example: the figure-eight datum over Q(√−3)
nodes.statement: For A_{4_1} = (1 1; 1 1), which is formal and not positive definite, the Nahm equations 1 − z_1 = −z_1z_2, 1 − z_2 = −z_1z_2 force z_1 = z_2 = z with z² − z + 1 = 0. So z = ζ_6, K = Q(√−3) of discriminant −3, δ = (2 − z)/z = −√−3 ≠ 0 (non-degenerate, N(δ) = 3), and ξ = 2[ζ_6] ∈ B(K), non-torsion (Bloch–Wigner value 2.0298832128 = vol(4_1)). With Δ divisible by 6 and by the primes of CGZ's M_K, and R = Z[ζ_6, 1/Δ], Theorem 5 gives f_{A,z} ∈ H_{R[δ^{-1/2}],ξ}|Δ. At m = 1, f_{A,z,1} = Φ(h) = (−3)^{−1/4}(1 + 11h/(72√−3) + 697h²/(1152(3√−3)²) + …) (GSWZ (1), §4.5, h = log(1 + x)). The symmetrisation is (−3)^{−1/2}(1 − (q − 1)²/27 + …) (GSWZ (2)), in H_{R[δ^{-1}]} = H_R. GSWZ (278): ⁴√−3·f̂(x)(1 + x)^{−1/24}(ζ_6²; 1 + x)³_∞(1 − ζ_6)^{−3/2} = 1 + (5ζ_6 − 7)x/3 + … is integral away from 3. K is abelian, so footnote 1 (with φ_m^{-1}, HabiroNumberFields/E20) and the Pochhammer generator ∏_j(q^{1/2}ζ^j; q)_∞^{n_j} of §1.5 apply.
hypotheses: A = (1 1; 1 1); z = (ζ_6, ζ_6); 6 | Δ, and Δ contains the primes of CGZ's M_K for K = Q(√−3) (for the symmetrisation Δ = 6 suffices).

The identification of f_{A,z} with the asymptotic series of the Kashaev invariant is GSWZ §4.5's statement ('with Φ^{4_1}_1(h) = f^{4_1}_1(x)'); its topological meaning is ArithmeticQuantumTopology's.

gaps.title: The periodicity of the Gaussian integrals is cited to two unread sources

The proof of Lemma 2.12 contains the essential computation, the endomorphism multiplying an m-th root of z by a root of unity permuting the integrals cyclically, and this packet records that as the proof outline. This is the single largest analytic obligation of the roadmap. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Vlasenko-Zwegers, Nahm's conjecture: asymptotic computations and counterexamples, and read pages 623 to 625; and record the N-dimensional lattice form as a library target. Revised by REV-HabiroNahmSeries (checker A): the earlier claim that Poisson summation is absent from the pinned libraries was false.

review.notes: Independent review of all 74 nodes, the baseline, the requests, gaps, coverage and restructure entries, and the suggested Lean file, by four checkers (HB.3-HB.4 with Garoufalidis-Zagier and CGZ Section 7; HB.5a-HB.5 with CGZ Sections 1.3 and 7 and the pinned modular-forms library; HB.8 with GSWZ Section 2; HB.9-HB.10 with GSWZ Sections 1.7, 3 and 4 and the packet-level fields), whose key numerical claims the reviewer re-checked with PARI/GP (the Euler-product phase behind GZ Theorem 3.1 to 60 digits, the solution order in CGZ Theorem 7.4, the level-2 counterexample to GSWZ Theorem 7, the Gauss-sum normalisation of GSWZ (43), 1/delta for A = (3), the quartic discriminant and G_4). Sources: CGZ arXiv v3, GSWZ arXiv v2 and GZ arXiv v1, each as PDF and e-print, hashes confirmed. Outcome: 71 nodes corrected, 38 added, 3 deleted (GZ's coefficient-versus-radial node, false as stated; the HB.9 p-adic polylogarithm node, which duplicated HabiroNumberFields HB.7; the HB.9 symmetrisation corollaries, which stated a false corollary and are split into correct nodes); 94 baseline declarations, each confirmed in the pinned index; every test has a kind; 63 source issues recorded (the packet had none). Main corrections: (1) false statements copied from the sources: GZ Theorem 3.1's root of unity chi (right only for alpha = 1/m) and its all-orders series (missing factor, wrong sign, psi not exponentiated), GZ Proposition 2.2 in four places, CGZ Theorem 7.1 without 'n odd', the sign of GZ's C_0(A), GSWZ Theorem 7 (level-m admissibility fails at Phi_d with m | d; corrected ring), the sign of U_m (67), the phase of (121), the Riccati system (89), the Hessian identity (169), the order-m q-difference sign, GSWZ (229) (off by t) and (280), and Corollary 1.10 (the constant term needs delta^{-1/2} and the Kummer root); (2) closure: the ratios and Riccati system, the congruence sums, the formal Pochhammer symbol, the Laurent expansion at a root of unity, the plethystic logarithm, the ring S, the Frobenius lift, the moment and Poisson lemmas, the Euler-Maclaurin remainder, the lemma that an invariant Nahm sum is a modular function, and the rank-one product identities had no nodes; (3) library: HB.5a re-planned Mathlib's arithmetic subgroups, cusps and widths, and the claim that Poisson summation is absent was false; (4) ownership and links: HabiroNumberFields HB.1/HB.2/HB.6/HB.7, QM.0 and HabiroRings HR.1 are cited by node id; the HB.10 exports (HR.6, HQ.5, HQ.8, QT.7) were consumers listed as prerequisites; the HC.1 and HC.2 requests were misdirected. Two dependency cycles created by the checkers' additions were broken by the reviewer (HB.5 meromorphy uses HB.4 at m = 1; the FGI collection is defined before its periodicity lemma). No stage-level or node-level cycle remains, including across roadmaps. Coverage: HB.5a decomposed, the other six stages partial, with 22 gaps and 9 stage-level requests. The packet is accepted: every node is corrected or added, every baseline citation is confirmed, and the open points are recorded.
